sanskrit: ajayad rājaputrāṃs tān yatamānān mahāraṇe ekaḥ pañcāśataṃ śatrūn sātyakiḥ satyavikramaḥ
english: Sātyaki, whose valour was unfailing, alone vanquished those princes who strove against him in the great battle—fifty foes laid low by his single hand.

sanskrit: saṃprāpya bhāratīmadhyaṃ talaghoṣasamākulam asiśaktigadāpūrṇam aplavaṃ salilaṃ yathā
english: He had reached the midst of the Bhārata host, loud with the clapping of palms, thronged with swords and spears and maces, like waters that offer no raft for crossing.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma śaineyacaritaṃ raṇe pratīcyāṃ diśi taṃ dṛṣṭvā prācyāṃ paśyāma lāghavāt
english: There in the fray we beheld the wondrous course of Śaineya: glimpsing him in the western quarter, by his swiftness we saw him next in the east.

sanskrit: udīcīṃ dakṣiṇāṃ prācīṃ pratīcīṃ prasṛtas tathā nṛtyann ivācarac chūro yathā rathaśataṃ tathā
english: North, south, east, and west he ranged, the hero moving as though he danced, as if he were a hundred chariots at once.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā caritaṃ tasya siṃhavikrāntagāminaḥ trigartāḥ saṃnyavartanta saṃtaptāḥ svajanaṃ prati
english: Beholding the feats of him who moved with the stride of a lion's prowess, the Trigartas turned back, anguished for their own kinsmen.

sanskrit: tam anye śūrasenānāṃ śūrāḥ saṃkhye nyavārayan niyacchantaḥ śaravrātair mattaṃ dvipam ivāṅkuśaiḥ
english: Then other warriors among the Śūrasenas checked him in the battle, restraining him with showers of arrows as goads restrain a maddened elephant.

sanskrit: tān nyavārayad āyastān muhūrtam iva sātyakiḥ tataḥ kaliṅgair yuyudhe so 'cintyabalavikramaḥ
english: Sātyaki, of inconceivable strength and valour, held those straining warriors off but a moment, and then did battle with the Kaliṅgas.

sanskrit: tāṃ ca senām atikramya kaliṅgānāṃ duratyayām atha pārthaṃ mahābāhur dhanaṃjayam upāsadat
english: Having passed beyond that host of the Kaliṅgas, hard to traverse, the mighty-armed one drew near to Pārtha Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: tarann iva jale śrānto yathā sthalam upeyivān taṃ dṛṣṭvā puruṣavyāghraṃ yuyudhānaḥ samāśvasat
english: As a swimmer wearied in the water gains the shore at last, so Yuyudhāna, seeing that tiger among men, took heart again.

sanskrit: tam āyāntam abhiprekṣya keśavo 'rjunam abravīt asāv āyāti śaineyas tava pārtha padānugaḥ
english: Beholding him approach, Keśava said to Arjuna: "Yonder comes Śaineya, O Pārtha, your follower in the field."

sanskrit: eṣa śiṣyaḥ sakhā caiva tava satyaparākramaḥ sarvān yodhāṃs tṛṇīkṛtya vijigye puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: "This is your disciple and your friend, whose prowess never fails; counting all those warriors as so much straw, that bull among men has conquered them."

sanskrit: eṣa kauravayodhānāṃ kṛtvā ghoram upadravam tava prāṇaiḥ priyataraḥ kirīṭinn eti sātyakiḥ
english: "Having wrought dread havoc among the Kaurava warriors, Sātyaki—dearer to you than your own breath, O Kirīṭin—now draws near."

sanskrit: eṣa droṇaṃ tathā bhojaṃ kṛtavarmāṇam eva ca kadarthīkṛtya viśikhaiḥ phalgunābhyeti sātyakiḥ
english: "Having brought low Droṇa, the Bhoja, and Kṛtavarman with his arrows, Sātyaki comes toward Phalguna."

sanskrit: dharmarājapriyānveṣī hatvā yodhān varān varān śūraś caiva kṛtāstraś ca phalgunābhyeti sātyakiḥ
english: "Seeking the welfare of the Dharma-king, having slain warrior after chosen warrior—a hero and a master of arms—Sātyaki comes toward Phalguna."

sanskrit: kṛtvā suduṣkaraṃ karma sainyamadhye mahābalaḥ tava darśanam anvicchan pāṇḍavābhyeti sātyakiḥ
english: "Having done a deed most hard to do in the midst of the host, the mighty one, longing to see you, comes toward the Pāṇḍava—Sātyaki draws near."

sanskrit: bahūn ekarathenājau yodhayitvā mahārathān ācāryapramukhān pārtha āyāty eṣa hi sātyakiḥ
english: "Having fought with a single chariot against many great car-warriors, foremost the Preceptor among them, this Sātyaki, O Pārtha, comes onward."

sanskrit: svabāhubalam āśritya vidārya ca varūthinīm preṣito dharmaputreṇa parthaiṣo 'bhyeti sātyakiḥ
english: "Relying on the strength of his own arms, having torn through the army, sent forth by the son of Dharma, this Sātyaki comes toward you, O Pārtha."

sanskrit: yasya nāsti samo yodhaḥ kauraveṣu kathaṃ cana so 'yam āyāti kaunteya sātyakiḥ satyavikramaḥ
english: "He to whom no warrior among the Kauravas is in any wise an equal—he, O Kaunteya, comes onward: Sātyaki of unfailing valour."

sanskrit: kurusainyād vimukto vai siṃho madhyād gavām iva nihatya bahulāḥ senāḥ pārthaiṣo 'bhyeti sātyakiḥ
english: "Loosed from the Kuru host like a lion from the midst of a herd of cattle, having slain whole armies, this Sātyaki comes toward you, O Pārtha."

sanskrit: eṣa rājasahasrāṇāṃ vaktraiḥ paṅkajasaṃnibhaiḥ āstīrya vasudhāṃ pārtha kṣipram āyāti sātyakiḥ
english: "Having strewn the earth with the lotus-like faces of thousands of kings, O Pārtha, Sātyaki comes swiftly on."

sanskrit: eṣa duryodhanaṃ jitvā bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaṃ raṇe nihatya jalasaṃdhaṃ ca kṣipram āyāti sātyakiḥ
english: "Having conquered Duryodhana together with his brothers in the battle, and slain Jalasaṃdha, Sātyaki comes swiftly on."

sanskrit: rudhiraughavatīṃ kṛtvā nadīṃ śoṇitakardamām tṛṇavan nyasya kauravyān eṣa āyāti sātyakiḥ
english: "Having made a river that runs in floods of blood, miry with gore, and cast down the Kauravas like so much grass, Sātyaki comes onward."

sanskrit: tato 'prahṛṣṭaḥ kaunteyaḥ keśavaṃ vākyam abravīt na me priyaṃ mahābāho yan mām abhyeti sātyakiḥ
english: Then the son of Kuntī, far from glad, spoke these words to Keśava: "It pleases me not, O mighty-armed one, that Sātyaki comes toward me."

sanskrit: na hi jānāmi vṛttāntaṃ dharmarājasya keśava sātvatena vihīnaḥ sa yadi jīvati vā na vā
english: "For I do not know the tidings of the Dharma-king, O Keśava—whether, bereft of the Sātvata, he yet lives or no."

sanskrit: etena hi mahābāho rakṣitavyaḥ sa pārthivaḥ tam eṣa katham utsṛjya mama kṛṣṇa padānugaḥ
english: "By him, O mighty-armed one, that king ought to have been guarded; how then, O Kṛṣṇa, has this my follower forsaken him?"

sanskrit: rājā droṇāya cotsṛṣṭaḥ saindhavaś cānipātitaḥ pratyudyātaś ca śaineyam eṣa bhūriśravā raṇe
english: "The king is left exposed to Droṇa, the Saindhava is not yet struck down, and this Bhūriśravas advances against Śaineya in the field."

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ gurutaro bhāraḥ saindhavān me samāhitaḥ jñātavyaś ca hi me rājā rakṣitavyaś ca sātyakiḥ
english: "Now this is a burden heavier than the Saindhava laid upon me: I must learn how the king fares, and I must protect Sātyaki."

sanskrit: jayadrathaś ca hantavyo lambate ca divākaraḥ śrāntaś caiṣa mahābāhur alpaprāṇaś ca sāṃpratam
english: "And Jayadratha must be slain, and the sun is sinking low; and this mighty-armed one is now wearied and short of breath."

sanskrit: pariśrāntā hayāś cāsya hayayantā ca mādhava na ca bhūriśravāḥ śrāntaḥ sasahāyaś ca keśava
english: "Spent are his horses, O Mādhava, and his driver too; but Bhūriśravas is not weary, and he has comrades at his side, O Keśava."

sanskrit: apīdānīṃ bhaved asya kṣemam asmin samāgame kaccin na sāgaraṃ tīrtvā sātyakiḥ satyavikramaḥ goṣpadaṃ prāpya sīdeta mahaujāḥ śinipuṃgavaḥ
english: "Might it now go well with him in this encounter? May Sātyaki of unfailing valour, that bull of Śini's line of mighty energy, not founder in a cow's hoofprint after crossing the very ocean!"

sanskrit: api kauravamukhyena kṛtāstreṇa mahātmanā sametya bhūriśravasā svastimān sātyakir bhavet
english: "May Sātyaki come through unharmed in his meeting with Bhūriśravas, that foremost of the Kauravas, a master of arms and a great soul."

sanskrit: vyatikramam imaṃ manye dharmarājasya keśava ācāryād bhayam utsṛjya yaḥ preṣayati sātyakim
english: "I count this a transgression on the part of the Dharma-king, O Keśava, who, casting aside his fear of the Preceptor, sends Sātyaki forth."

sanskrit: grahaṇaṃ dharmarājasya khagaḥ śyena ivāmiṣam nityam āśaṃsate droṇaḥ kaccit syāt kuśalī nṛpaḥ
english: "Droṇa forever yearns to seize the Dharma-king, as a hawk on the wing yearns for its prey. Is the king, I wonder, yet safe?"

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya sātvataṃ yuddhadurmadam krodhād bhūriśravā rājan sahasā samupādravat
english: Saṃjaya said: Beholding that Sātvata, frenzied for battle, rushing on, Bhūriśravas, O king, in his wrath charged against him at once.

sanskrit: tam abravīn mahābāhuḥ kauravyaḥ śinipuṃgavam adya prāpto 'si diṣṭyā me cakṣurviṣayam ity uta
english: The mighty-armed Kaurava spoke to that bull of Śini's line: "By good fortune you have come this day within the range of my sight!"

sanskrit: cirābhilaṣitaṃ kāmam adya prāpsyāmi saṃyuge na hi me mokṣyase jīvan yadi notsṛjase raṇam
english: "The desire long cherished I shall fulfil this day in combat; you shall not escape me alive unless you abandon the fight."

sanskrit: adya tvāṃ samare hatvā nityaṃ śūrābhimāninam nandayiṣyāmi dāśārha kururājaṃ suyodhanam
english: "Slaying you this day in battle—you who ever account yourself a hero, O Dāśārha—I shall gladden Suyodhana, king of the Kurus."

sanskrit: adya madbāṇanirdagdhaṃ patitaṃ dharaṇītale drakṣyatas tvāṃ raṇe vīrau sahitau keśavārjunau
english: "This day, scorched by my shafts and fallen to the earth, you shall the two heroes Keśava and Arjuna behold together in the field."

sanskrit: adya dharmasuto rājā śrutvā tvāṃ nihataṃ mayā savrīḍo bhavitā sadyo yenāsīha praveśitaḥ
english: "This day the king, the son of Dharma, by whom you were sent into this fray, hearing that you have been slain by me, shall at once be filled with shame."

sanskrit: adya me vikramaṃ pārtho vijñāsyati dhanaṃjayaḥ tvayi bhūmau vinihate śayāne rudhirokṣite
english: "This day shall Pārtha Dhanaṃjaya know my prowess, when you lie struck down upon the earth, drenched in blood."

sanskrit: cirābhilaṣito hy adya tvayā saha samāgamaḥ purā devāsure yuddhe śakrasya balinā yathā
english: "This meeting with you, long desired, is come to me this day, as of old in the war of gods and demons the encounter of Śakra with Bali."

sanskrit: adya yuddhaṃ mahāghoraṃ tava dāsyāmi sātvata tato jñāsyasi tattvena madvīryabalapauruṣam
english: "This day I shall give you most dreadful battle, O Sātvata; then shall you know in truth my valour, my strength, and my manhood."

sanskrit: adya saṃyamanīṃ yātā mayā tvaṃ nihato raṇe yathā rāmānujenājau rāvaṇir lakṣmaṇena vai
english: "This day, slain by me in battle, you shall fare to the city of Yama, as in the fray Rāvaṇa's son was slain by Lakṣmaṇa, the younger brother of Rāma."

sanskrit: adya kṛṣṇaś ca pārthaś ca dharmarājaś ca mādhava hate tvayi nirutsāhā raṇaṃ tyakṣyanty asaṃśayam
english: "This day, O Mādhava, when you are slain, Kṛṣṇa and Pārtha and the Dharma-king, robbed of all heart, shall doubtless abandon the battle."

sanskrit: adya te 'pacitiṃ kṛtvā śitair mādhava sāyakaiḥ tatstriyo nandayiṣyāmi ye tvayā nihatā raṇe
english: "This day, O Mādhava, having taken vengeance upon you with whetted shafts, I shall gladden the women of those whom you slew in the field."

sanskrit: cakṣurviṣayasaṃprāpto na tvaṃ mādhava mokṣyase siṃhasya viṣayaṃ prāpto yathā kṣudramṛgas tathā
english: "Come within the range of my sight, O Mādhava, you shall not escape, even as a little deer that has come within a lion's reach."

sanskrit: yuyudhānas tu taṃ rājan pratyuvāca hasann iva kauraveya na saṃtrāso vidyate mama saṃyuge
english: But Yuyudhāna, O king, answered him as though laughing: "O scion of Kuru, no terror dwells in me amid combat."

sanskrit: sa māṃ nihanyāt saṃgrāme yo māṃ kuryān nirāyudham samās tu śāśvatīr hanyād yo māṃ hanyād dhi saṃyuge
english: "He alone could slay me in battle who first could leave me weaponless; and he who would slay me in combat must strive through unending years to do it."

sanskrit: kiṃ mṛṣoktena bahunā karmaṇā tu samācara śāradasyeva meghasya garjitaṃ niṣphalaṃ hi te
english: "What use this much idle talk? Set to the deed itself! Your thunder is as barren as that of an autumn cloud."

sanskrit: śrutvaitad garjitaṃ vīra hāsyaṃ hi mama jāyate cirakālepsitaṃ loke yuddham adyāstu kaurava
english: "Hearing this thundering of yours, O hero, laughter rises in me. Let the battle long desired in this world be ours this day, O Kaurava!"

sanskrit: tvarate me matis tāta tvayi yuddhābhikāṅkṣiṇi nāhatvā saṃnivartiṣye tvām adya puruṣādhama
english: "My mind hastens eagerly, sir, now that you long for battle. I shall not turn back this day, O basest of men, until I have slain you."

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ tau tadā vāgbhis takṣantau narapuṃgavau jighāṃsū paramakruddhāv abhijaghnatur āhave
english: Then those two bulls among men, gashing one another with words, athirst to kill and wrought to utmost fury, fell upon each other in the fray.

sanskrit: sametau tau naravyāghrau śuṣmiṇau spardhinau raṇe dviradāv iva saṃkruddhau vāśitārthe madotkaṭau
english: Those two tigers among men, fierce and rivalrous, met in the battle like two enraged elephants frenzied with rut, contending for a she-elephant.

sanskrit: bhūriśravāḥ sātyakiś ca vavarṣatur ariṃdamau śaravarṣāṇi bhīmāni meghāv iva parasparam
english: Bhūriśravas and Sātyaki, those tamers of foes, rained dreadful showers of arrows upon each other like two storm-clouds.

sanskrit: saumadattis tu śaineyaṃ pracchādyeṣubhir āśugaiḥ jighāṃsur bharataśreṣṭha vivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: The son of Somadatta, O best of the Bharatas, veiling Śaineya with swift-flying shafts and athirst to slay him, pierced him with whetted arrows.

sanskrit: daśabhiḥ sātyakiṃ viddhvā saumadattir athāparān mumoca niśitān bāṇāñ jighāṃsuḥ śinipuṃgavam
english: Having pierced Sātyaki with ten shafts, the son of Somadatta then let fly yet more keen arrows, eager to slay that bull of Śini's line.

sanskrit: tān asya viśikhāṃs tīkṣṇān antarikṣe viśāṃ pate aprāptān astramāyābhir agrasat sātyakiḥ prabho
english: Those sharp arrows of his, O lord of peoples, Sātyaki devoured in mid-air by the magic of his weapons, O mighty one, before ever they reached him.

sanskrit: tau pṛthak śaravarṣābhyām avarṣetāṃ parasparam uttamābhijanau vīrau kuruvṛṣṇiyaśaskarau
english: Each of those two heroes of noblest birth, who brought glory upon the Kuru and the Vṛṣṇi lines, rained showers of arrows upon the other.

sanskrit: tau nakhair iva śārdūlau dantair iva mahādvipau rathaśaktibhir anyonyaṃ viśikhaiś cāpy akṛntatām
english: As two tigers with their claws, as two great elephants with their tusks, so did they rend each other with chariot-spears and with arrows.

sanskrit: nirbhidantau hi gātrāṇi vikṣarantau ca śoṇitam vyaṣṭambhayetām anyonyaṃ prāṇadyūtābhidevinau
english: Piercing each other's limbs and pouring forth their blood, they held one another at bay, gamblers staking life itself in the play.

sanskrit: evam uttamakarmāṇau kuruvṛṣṇiyaśaskarau parasparam ayudhyetāṃ vāraṇāv iva yūthapau
english: Thus those two of supreme deeds, who brought glory upon the Kuru and the Vṛṣṇi lines, fought one against the other like two leaders of elephant herds.

sanskrit: tāv adīrgheṇa kālena brahmalokapuraskṛtau jigīṣantau paraṃ sthānam anyonyam abhijaghnatuḥ
english: In no long time, with the world of Brahmā set before them, each striving to win the supreme abode, they smote upon one another.

sanskrit: sātyakiḥ saumadattiś ca śaravṛṣṭyā parasparam hṛṣṭavad dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ paśyatām abhyavarṣatām
english: Sātyaki and the son of Somadatta rained shafts upon each other as though in joy, while the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra looked on.

sanskrit: saṃpraikṣanta janās tatra yudhyamānau yudhāṃ patī yūthapau vāśitāhetoḥ prayuddhāv iva kuñjarau
english: The hosts gazed there upon those two lords of warriors as they fought, like two herd-bull elephants battling for the sake of a she-elephant.

sanskrit: anyonyasya hayān hatvā dhanuṣī vinikṛtya ca virathāv asiyuddhāya sameyātāṃ mahāraṇe
english: Having slain each other's horses and cut apart each other's bows, the two, bereft of their chariots, closed for sword-combat in that great battle.

sanskrit: ārṣabhe carmaṇī citre pragṛhya vipule śubhe vikośau cāpy asī kṛtvā samare tau viceratuḥ
english: Taking up their broad and gleaming shields of bull's hide, bright with figures, and drawing their swords from the scabbard, the two ranged about the field.

sanskrit: carantau vividhān mārgān maṇḍalāni ca bhāgaśaḥ muhur ājaghnatuḥ kruddhāv anyonyam arimardanau
english: Moving along varied tracks and through their circling figures one by one, those crushers of foes in their wrath struck again and again at each other.

sanskrit: sakhaḍgau citravarmāṇau saniṣkāṅgadabhūṣaṇau raṇe raṇotkaṭau rājann anyonyaṃ paryakarṣatām
english: Swords in hand, in figured mail, adorned with golden necklets and armlets, those two who exulted in war, O king, dragged each other to and fro in the battle.

sanskrit: muhūrtam iva rājendra parikṛṣya parasparam paśyatāṃ sarvasainyānāṃ vīrāv āśvasatāṃ punaḥ
english: For a while, O lord of kings, having hauled each other about before the gaze of all the hosts, the two heroes drew breath again.

sanskrit: asibhyāṃ carmaṇī śubhre vipule ca śarāvare nikṛtya puruṣavyāghrau bāhuyuddhaṃ pracakratuḥ
english: Having hewn apart with their swords the bright broad shields that warded off the shafts, those two tigers among men set themselves to wrestling with bare arms.

sanskrit: vyūḍhoraskau dīrghabhujau niyuddhakuśalāv ubhau bāhubhiḥ samasajjetām āyasaiḥ parighair iva
english: Broad-chested and long-armed, both skilled in the wrestler's art, they grappled with their arms as though with bars of iron.

sanskrit: tayor āsan bhujāghātā nigrahapragrahau tathā śikṣābalasamudbhūtāḥ sarvayodhapraharṣaṇāḥ
english: Their blows of arm, their grips and counter-grips, sprung from skill and strength, were a delight to all the warriors there.

sanskrit: tayor nṛvarayo rājan samare yudhyamānayoḥ bhīmo 'bhavan mahāśabdo vajraparvatayor iva
english: As those two best of men contended in the field, O king, there arose a fearful, mighty din, as of mountains of adamant.

sanskrit: dvipāv iva viṣāṇāgraiḥ śṛṅgair iva maharṣabhau yuyudhāte mahātmānau kurusātvatapuṃgavau
english: Like two elephants with the points of their tusks, like two great bulls with their horns, those high-souled bulls of the Kuru and Sātvata lines did battle.

sanskrit: kṣīṇāyudhe sātvate yudhyamāne; tato 'bravīd arjunaṃ vāsudevaḥ paśyasvainaṃ virathaṃ yudhyamānaṃ; raṇe ketuṃ sarvadhanurdharāṇām
english: As the Sātvata fought on, his weapons now spent, Vāsudeva spoke then to Arjuna: "Behold him fighting without his chariot in the fray—the banner of all who bear the bow!"

sanskrit: praviṣṭo bhāratīṃ senāṃ tava pāṇḍava pṛṣṭhataḥ yodhitaś ca mahāvīryaiḥ sarvair bhārata bhārataiḥ
english: "He entered the Bhārata host at your back, O Pāṇḍava, and was set upon by all the Bharatas of mighty valour, O scion of Bharata."

sanskrit: pariśrānto yudhāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ saṃprāpto bhūridakṣiṇam yuddhakāṅkṣiṇam āyāntaṃ naitat samam ivārjuna
english: "Worn out, that best of warriors has come upon Bhūriśravas, who advances athirst for battle. This is no even match, O Arjuna."

sanskrit: tato bhūriśravāḥ kruddhaḥ sātyakiṃ yuddhadurmadam udyamya nyahanad rājan matto mattam iva dvipam
english: Then Bhūriśravas in his wrath, O king, lifting up Sātyaki, who was frenzied for the fight, dashed him down as a maddened elephant dashes down another in rut.

sanskrit: rathasthayor dvayor yuddhe kruddhayor yodhamukhyayoḥ keśavārjunayo rājan samare prekṣamāṇayoḥ
english: Even as those two foremost of warriors, Keśava and Arjuna, stationed wrathful upon their chariot, looked on at the battle, O king—

sanskrit: atha kṛṣṇo mahābāhur arjunaṃ pratyabhāṣata paśya vṛṣṇyandhakavyāghraṃ saumadattivaśaṃ gatam
english: —then mighty-armed Kṛṣṇa spoke again to Arjuna: "See, that tiger of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas has fallen into the power of Somadatta's son!"
